---
title: "The command-line runner"
subtitle: "`src/run.ts`: long runs without a browser"
---

Long runs belong on the command line: 600 000 steps take about an hour on one core, and several
runs with different seeds can go in parallel, one per core. The runner creates a simulation, steps
it, and writes the recorded states to disk. Optionally it measures overlaps at every snapshot and
logs the time per step.

```sh
node build/run.js --steps 600000 --seed 7 --out output/states.json
node build/run.js --steps 30000 --set rate=0.002 --set anchorMaxStretch=1
node build/run.js --steps 60000 --overlap-log output/overlap.csv --overlap-check
```

It is careful about two things. A run can take hours, so it never loses the work done so far:
the file is saved regularly, always completely, and also when the run is interrupted or the physics
engine fails. And it fails early: a mistyped option or an unwritable output path is reported
before the first step, not after the last.

```{.typescript #cli-imports}
import * as fs from "node:fs";
import * as path from "node:path";
import { DEFAULT_PARAMS, SimulationParams } from "./model.js";
import {
  OVERLAP_CSV_HEADER, OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION, OVERLAP_WARMUP_STEPS, OverlapMeter, OverlapStats, overlapCsvRow,
} from "./overlap.js";
import { Simulation, rapierVersion } from "./simulation.js";
```

## Options

The help text documents every option. Progress goes to standard error, so standard output stays
free for `--list-params`.

```{.typescript #cli-usage}
const USAGE = `Usage: node build/run.js --steps N [options]

Options:
  --steps N         number of simulation steps to run (required)
  --out FILE        output file (default: states.json)
  --seed N          random seed (default: random; printed at start)
  --save-every N    also save after every N snapshots (default: 500; 0 = only at the end)
  --set KEY=VALUE   override a simulation parameter (repeatable), e.g. --set rate=0.002
  --list-params     print all parameters with their defaults and exit
  --help            show this help

Overlap check (cell-cell penetration depth, measured at every snapshot):
  --overlap-log FILE         write one CSV row per snapshot (max/mean/p99 depth, ...)
  --overlap-warmup N         steps to let the random initial placement relax before the
                             target applies (default: ${OVERLAP_WARMUP_STEPS})
  --overlap-target F         target: max depth < F * cell width (default: ${OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION})
  --overlap-check            exit with status 3 if the target is missed after the warm-up

Performance:
  --timing-log FILE          write one CSV row per snapshot: step, cells, ms per step since the last snapshot

The file is rewritten in full at each save, so it is always a complete, valid JSON file.
Parameters, seed and progress are printed to stderr.`;
```

Any mistake ends the program with the message and the help text, and exit status 1:

```{.typescript #cli-fail}
function fail(message: string): never {
  console.error(`Error: ${message}\n\n${USAGE}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
```

`parseArgs` walks the arguments once. Two small helpers read an option's value and check that it
is a non-negative integer. `--set` accepts any parameter of [the model](model.qmd#parameters) by
name, checked against `DEFAULT_PARAMS`, so new parameters need no change here. `--list-params` and
`--help` print and exit at once.

```{.typescript #cli-parse-args}
function parseArgs(argv: string[]) {
  const opts = {
    steps: NaN, out: "states.json", saveEvery: 500,
    overrides: {} as Partial<SimulationParams>,
    overlapLog: null as string | null, overlapWarmup: OVERLAP_WARMUP_STEPS, overlapTarget: OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION,
    overlapCheck: false, timingLog: null as string | null,
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
    const arg = argv[i];
    const value = (): string => {
      if (i + 1 >= argv.length) { fail(`${arg} needs a value`); }
      return argv[++i];
    };
    const int = (s: string): number => {
      const n = Number(s);
      if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 0) { fail(`${arg} expects a non-negative integer, got "${s}"`); }
      return n;
    };
    switch (arg) {
      case "--steps": opts.steps = int(value()); break;
      case "--out": opts.out = value(); break;
      case "--seed": opts.overrides.seed = int(value()); break;
      case "--save-every": opts.saveEvery = int(value()); break;
      case "--set": {
        const [key, raw] = value().split("=");
        if (!(key in DEFAULT_PARAMS)) { fail(`unknown parameter "${key}" (see --list-params)`); }
        const num = Number(raw);
        if (raw === undefined || raw === "" || Number.isNaN(num)) { fail(`--set ${key} needs a numeric value`); }
        (opts.overrides as Record<string, number>)[key] = num;
        break;
      }
      case "--overlap-log": opts.overlapLog = value(); break;
      case "--overlap-warmup": opts.overlapWarmup = int(value()); break;
      case "--overlap-target": {
        const raw = value();
        opts.overlapTarget = Number(raw);
        if (!(opts.overlapTarget > 0)) { fail(`--overlap-target expects a positive number, got "${raw}"`); }
        break;
      }
      case "--overlap-check": opts.overlapCheck = true; break;
      case "--timing-log": opts.timingLog = value(); break;
      case "--list-params":
        for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(DEFAULT_PARAMS)) { console.log(`${k}=${v}`); }
        process.exit(0);
      case "--help": case "-h":
        console.log(USAGE);
        process.exit(0);
      default:
        fail(`unknown option "${arg}"`);
    }
  }
  if (Number.isNaN(opts.steps)) { fail("--steps is required"); }
  if (opts.overlapCheck && !opts.overlapLog) { fail("--overlap-check needs --overlap-log"); }
  return opts;
}
```

## Saving

The states file is written piece by piece (see [Writing the file](recording.qmd#writing-the-file))
to a temporary file, which then replaces the real one. Renaming is atomic, so even if the program is
killed while saving, the states file on disk is always the previous complete version or the new
complete version, never half of one.

```{.typescript #cli-save}
function save(sim: Simulation, out: string): void {
  const tmp = `${out}.tmp`;
  const fd = fs.openSync(tmp, "w");
  try {
    for (const piece of sim.states.toPieces()) { fs.writeSync(fd, piece); }
  } finally {
    fs.closeSync(fd);
  }
  fs.renameSync(tmp, out);
  const mb = fs.statSync(out).size / 1e6;
  console.error(`  saved ${sim.states.snapshotCount} snapshots, ${sim.states.idCount} ids -> ${out} (${mb.toFixed(1)} MB)`);
}
```

A short duration format for the progress reports, such as `1h38m` or `4m05s`:

```{.typescript #cli-format-duration}
function formatDuration(seconds: number): string {
  const h = Math.floor(seconds / 3600), m = Math.floor((seconds % 3600) / 60), s = Math.floor(seconds % 60);
  return h > 0 ? `${h}h${String(m).padStart(2, "0")}m` : m > 0 ? `${m}m${String(s).padStart(2, "0")}s` : `${s}s`;
}
```

## The run

```{.typescript #cli-main}
async function main(): Promise<void> {
  <<cli-prepare>>

  <<cli-overlap-setup>>

  <<cli-timing-setup>>

  <<cli-loop>>

  <<cli-finish>>
}
```

### Before the first step

The output folders are created, and the states file is tested for writing by creating and deleting
its temporary file, so that a bad path fails now rather than at the first save, possibly hours
later. Then the simulation is created; invalid parameters stop the run here too. The first line of
output records the Rapier version, the seed and the run's length, and any parameters that were
changed, which is everything needed to repeat the run.

```{.typescript #cli-prepare}
const opts = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
const out = path.resolve(opts.out);
try {
  for (const file of [out, opts.overlapLog, opts.timingLog]) {
    if (file) { fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(path.resolve(file)), { recursive: true }); }
  }
  fs.closeSync(fs.openSync(`${out}.tmp`, "w"));
  fs.unlinkSync(`${out}.tmp`);
} catch (e) {
  fail(`cannot write ${out}: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`);
}
let sim: Simulation;
try {
  sim = await Simulation.create(opts.overrides);
} catch (e) {
  fail(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
}

console.error(`Rapier ${rapierVersion()}, seed ${sim.params.seed}, ${opts.steps} steps, snapshot every ${sim.params.snapshotInterval} steps -> ${out}`);
const changed = Object.entries(opts.overrides).filter(([k]) => k !== "seed");
if (changed.length > 0) { console.error(`overrides: ${changed.map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`).join(", ")}`); }
```

With `--overlap-log`, the [overlap meter](overlap.qmd) runs at every snapshot. The runner keeps the
latest measurement for the progress reports and, after the warm-up, counts the snapshots and those
over the target, sums the mean depths, and remembers the worst snapshot.

```{.typescript #cli-overlap-setup}
const width = 2 * sim.params.radius;
const targetDepth = opts.overlapTarget * width;
const meter = new OverlapMeter();
let overlapFd: number | null = null;
let last: OverlapStats | null = null;
let worst: OverlapStats | null = null;
let snapshotsChecked = 0, snapshotsOverTarget = 0, meanSum = 0;
if (opts.overlapLog) {
  overlapFd = fs.openSync(path.resolve(opts.overlapLog), "w");
  fs.writeSync(overlapFd, OVERLAP_CSV_HEADER + "\n");
  console.error(`overlap: logging to ${path.resolve(opts.overlapLog)}; target max depth < ${opts.overlapTarget} x width ` +
    `= ${targetDepth.toFixed(3)} after step ${opts.overlapWarmup}`);
}
```

With `--timing-log`, the time spent in `sim.step()` is summed between snapshots. Only the physics
is timed: saving and the overlap measurement are excluded.

```{.typescript #cli-timing-setup}
let timingFd: number | null = null;
let stepMs = 0, stepsTimed = 0;
if (opts.timingLog) {
  timingFd = fs.openSync(path.resolve(opts.timingLog), "w");
  fs.writeSync(timingFd, "step,cells,ms_per_step\n");
}
```

### The loop

Ctrl+C does not kill the run: it sets a flag, and the loop stops after the current step and saves.

```{.typescript #cli-loop}
let interrupted = false;
process.on("SIGINT", () => { interrupted = true; });

const start = Date.now();
let lastReport = start;
let savedAtSnapshot = -1;
for (let i = 0; i < opts.steps && !interrupted; i++) {
  <<cli-step>>
  <<cli-log-timing>>
  <<cli-log-overlap>>
  <<cli-periodic-save>>
  <<cli-progress>>
}
```

Each step is timed. If the physics engine throws (a WebAssembly trap, for instance, when its memory
runs out), the snapshots recorded so far are saved before the program exits with status 4.

```{.typescript #cli-step}
const t0 = performance.now();
let snapshotTaken: boolean;
try {
  snapshotTaken = sim.step();
} catch (e) {
  console.error(`ERROR: the simulation failed at step ${sim.stepCount + 1}:`, e);
  console.error(`saving the ${sim.states.snapshotCount} snapshots recorded so far...`);
  save(sim, out);
  if (overlapFd !== null) { fs.closeSync(overlapFd); }
  if (timingFd !== null) { fs.closeSync(timingFd); }
  process.exit(4);
}
stepMs += performance.now() - t0;
stepsTimed++;
```

At each snapshot: the mean time per step since the last snapshot,

```{.typescript #cli-log-timing}
if (snapshotTaken && timingFd !== null) {
  fs.writeSync(timingFd, `${sim.stepCount},${sim.cellCount},${(stepMs / stepsTimed).toFixed(4)}\n`);
  stepMs = 0;
  stepsTimed = 0;
}
```

the overlap measurement and, after the warm-up, its statistics,

```{.typescript #cli-log-overlap}
if (snapshotTaken && overlapFd !== null) {
  last = meter.measure(sim, sim.params.radius, targetDepth);
  fs.writeSync(overlapFd, overlapCsvRow(last, width) + "\n");
  if (sim.stepCount >= opts.overlapWarmup) {
    snapshotsChecked++;
    meanSum += last.meanDepth;
    if (last.maxDepth >= targetDepth) { snapshotsOverTarget++; }
    if (!worst || last.maxDepth > worst.maxDepth) { worst = last; }
  }
}
```

and, every `--save-every` snapshots, a save:

```{.typescript #cli-periodic-save}
if (snapshotTaken && opts.saveEvery > 0 && sim.states.snapshotCount % opts.saveEvery === 0) {
  save(sim, out);
  savedAtSnapshot = sim.states.snapshotCount;
}
```

Every ten seconds of wall-clock time, a progress line reports the step, the cell and snapshot
counts, the speed, the estimated time to completion and the latest overlap:

```{.typescript #cli-progress}
const now = Date.now();
if (now - lastReport >= 10000) {
  lastReport = now;
  const elapsed = (now - start) / 1000;
  const rate = sim.stepCount / elapsed;
  const eta = (opts.steps - sim.stepCount) / rate;
  const overlap = last ? `, overlap max ${(last.maxDepth / width * 100).toFixed(1)}% / mean ${(last.meanDepth / width * 100).toFixed(2)}% of width` : "";
  console.error(`step ${sim.stepCount}/${opts.steps} (${(100 * sim.stepCount / opts.steps).toFixed(1)}%), ` +
    `${sim.cellCount} cells, ${sim.states.snapshotCount} snapshots, ${rate.toFixed(0)} steps/s, ETA ${formatDuration(eta)}${overlap}`);
}
```

### After the last step

The final save is skipped if nothing was recorded since the last one. With an overlap log, the run
ends with a verdict: the worst snapshot after the warm-up, the average mean depth, and how many
snapshots exceeded the target. With `--overlap-check`, a missed target sets exit status 3, so that
scripts can tell a run that finished from a run that also passed.

```{.typescript #cli-finish}
if (interrupted) { console.error(`interrupted at step ${sim.stepCount}; saving...`); }
if (sim.states.snapshotCount !== savedAtSnapshot) { save(sim, out); }
const seconds = (Date.now() - start) / 1000;
console.error(`done in ${formatDuration(seconds)}, ${(sim.stepCount / seconds).toFixed(0)} steps/s average, ` +
  `${sim.cellCount} cells at the end (seed ${sim.params.seed})`);

if (timingFd !== null) { fs.closeSync(timingFd); }
if (overlapFd !== null) {
  fs.closeSync(overlapFd);
  const pct = (d: number) => `${(d / width * 100).toFixed(2)}% of width (${d.toFixed(4)})`;
  if (snapshotsChecked === 0) {
    console.error(`overlap: no snapshots after the warm-up (step ${opts.overlapWarmup})`);
  } else {
    const passed = snapshotsOverTarget === 0;
    console.error(`overlap after step ${opts.overlapWarmup}: ${snapshotsChecked} snapshots, worst max depth ${pct(worst!.maxDepth)} ` +
      `at step ${worst!.step}, average mean depth ${pct(meanSum / snapshotsChecked)}, ` +
      `${snapshotsOverTarget} snapshots over target -> ${passed ? "PASS" : "FAIL"}`);
    if (!passed && opts.overlapCheck) { process.exitCode = 3; }
  }
}
```
